title: act-mcp .evidence JSONL record (schema_version 1)
description: One line of a <workspace>/.evidence/{benchmark,coverage}/<full-sha>/<run_id>.jsonl file: exactly one compact JSON object per line, LF-terminated. This schema describes a SINGLE LINE (one record), not a file. Normative prose lives in docs/adr/0002-evidence-jsonl-contract.md; if the two disagree, the ADR is wrong and must be fixed in the same change. Policy: a field is either present with the correct type or ABSENT. Explicit JSON null is never written and never valid, except where a property is declared with type [x, null] (currently: none). 'unknown' is expressed by omission, never by a sentinel value.

relpath.description: Workspace-relative path with '/' separators. No leading '/', no '~', and no '.' or '..' segments (a segment may start with up to two dots only if a non-dot character follows, so '.evidence' is fine and '..' is not). Absolute host paths must never appear in evidence.

schema_version.description: Record contract version. Writers only ever emit the version they were built with; readers MUST refuse a version they do not know how to read (see ADR-0002 section 7).

kind.description: CLOSED enum: the record variant, and therefore the directory the record is filed under. Unknown kind is a hard validation error, never a tolerated unknown value.

run_id.description: The act-mcp run this record came from. Lexicographically sortable: the UTC timestamp prefix is what makes .evidence/<kind>/<sha>/<run_id>.jsonl list in chronological order. Generated per ADR-0004; the shape is pinned here because the layout depends on it. Example: 20261110T004203Z-a1b2c3

commit.description: Full lowercase hex object id of the commit the run is attributed to (ADR-0003). Always 40 chars (or 64 for sha256 repos); short SHAs are forbidden because the path and this field are the join key the cross-commit scan relies on.

workflow.description: Workflow identity as resolved by the workspace validator: the workflow file basename without its .yml/.yaml extension (e.g. 'benchmark' for .github/workflows/benchmark.yml). Never an absolute or host path.

task.description: Job id inside the workflow that was run (act -j <job>). Never re-derived from logs; it is the resolved value from the tool call.

category.description: OPEN vocabulary: the classification that caused evidence to be written at all (only benchmark and coverage produce evidence). Consumers MUST tolerate values they do not know. In v1 category always equals kind.

run_status.description: Outcome of the act run that produced this record: success (act exited 0), failed (act ran, workflow exited non-zero), cancelled, timed_out, error (act could not be run / internal failure). Evidence from non-success runs is written, not suppressed; aggregators filter on this field.

tool.description: Producer identity. Optional act_version records the nektos/act version that ran, because an act upgrade moves timings and log shapes.

act_version.description: First version token of 'act --version', e.g. 0.2.68. Omitted when act did not report a version.

started_at.description: UTC start of the act run, RFC 3339 instant, always 'Z' (never '+00:00'), fractional seconds optional. Writers canonicalise to millisecond precision.

duration_ms.description: Wall duration of the whole act run in milliseconds. Omitted when the run never started or the duration is unknown; never 0 as a stand-in for unknown.

exit_code.description: act process exit status (wait(2) code, 0..=255). Omitted when act produced no exit status (killed by signal before exit, spawn failure).

host.description: Hostname of the machine that ran act (gethostname, lowercased). Advisory: useful for telling two workstations apart, never used as a join key.

flags.description: OPEN vocabulary of machine-readable caveats. Consumers MUST ignore flags they do not know; each known flag is listed in ADR-0002 section 5. 'unit_missing' is mandatory on a benchmark record whose job reported no unit.

name.description: benchmark: the metric name, verbatim from the job (or one of the built-in act-log names job_duration_s / step_duration_s). coverage: optional human label ('total' for a total record); the identity of a file record is 'path', not 'name'.

value.description: benchmark: the measured value. Any finite JSON number; negative values are allowed for deltas but never for *_s durations (that is an extractor rule, not a schema rule). NaN/Infinity are not expressible in JSON and must be rejected before serialization.

unit.description: benchmark: measurement unit, passed through VERBATIM from the job; act-mcp never converts or invents units. Omitted (and flags MUST contain 'unit_missing') when the job did not report one, so consumers can tell 'dimensionless/not reported' from a real unit and MUST NOT combine values with differing units. Preferred vocabulary is advisory: s, ms, us, ns, B, %, count, ops/s.

labels.description: benchmark: flat, ordered-by-convention grouping keys. Values are ALWAYS strings (numbers and booleans are stringified) so downstream group-by never has to type-switch. Known keys: job, step, os, runner, matrix, attempt, workflow, task. Open key set.

sample.description: benchmark: 1-based sample index, present ONLY when a job legitimately emitted more than one sample for the same (name, labels) pair. Two records with an identical (name, labels, value, source) tuple and no sample field is a writer bug: within one run the writer de-duplicates accidental repeats and numbers real ones.

scope.description: coverage: aggregation level of this record. 'total' is the workspace/run total, 'file' is one source file.

path.description: coverage (scope=file): the source file this record describes, workspace-relative with forward slashes, no leading '/', no '.' or '..' segments, no home or absolute host paths. Container-side paths (act mounts the workspace at /srv) are normalised back to workspace-relative before writing.

lines_found.description: coverage: denominator for line coverage. Present on every record parsed from a real coverage file; 0 means 'no measurable lines', which is NOT 0% coverage (ADR-0002 section 4 pins the consumer rule). Omitted only on percent-only scraped records.

lines_hit.description: coverage: numerator for line coverage. MUST be <= lines_found.

branches_found.description: coverage: branch denominator. Optional, but always paired with branches_hit (a source format that reports one reports both).

branches_hit.description: coverage: branch numerator. MUST be <= branches_found.

statements_found.description: coverage: statement denominator. Istanbul statements are a different unit from lines; keep them in their own pair and never average the two.

statements_hit.description: coverage: statement numerator. MUST be <= statements_found.

functions_found.description: coverage: function denominator (istanbul 'functions'). Reserved for formats that report it; optional and always paired with functions_hit.

functions_hit.description: coverage: function numerator. MUST be <= functions_found.

reported_percent.description: coverage: ONLY for sources that report a percentage and no raw counts (last-resort log scraping). Raw numerators are the contract; a denominator must never be invented to go with a scraped ratio, so a record carrying reported_percent MUST NOT carry any *_found/*_hit pair, and MUST carry flag 'percent_only'. Consumers MUST NOT silently mix percent-only records into raw history (ADR-0002 section 4).

reported_measure.description: coverage: which measure reported_percent refers to, because a scraped 'Coverage: 87.4%' line does not always say. Required with reported_percent; use 'unknown' rather than guessing.

source.description: How this record was produced. benchmark: job_file (payload file the job wrote through the bind mount), in_band_stdout (ACTMCP_BENCHMARK marker scraped from act's JSON log), act_log (timing derived from act's own job/step timings). coverage: lcov, coverage_summary (istanbul coverage-summary.json), log_scrape (last-resort percentage scraped from act's log; low confidence). File-based sources always outrank log scraping for the same scope.

source_path.description: Where the extractor read this number from, as a workspace-relative path (never an absolute host path). Required when source is job_file / lcov / coverage_summary; omitted for act_log, in_band_stdout and log_scrape (whose input is the act JSON log).

extra.description: Advisory passthrough: whatever the job or the parser kept for humans (tool output snippets, parser notes, percentage-only markers). Nothing in act-mcp or in downstream scanners may depend on a key here; anything load-bearing must become a real field.

allOf.description: A benchmark metric with no unit must say so, so consumers can tell 'no unit reported' from a real unit instead of guessing.

then.description: flags must be present and must name the caveat; 'absent flags' never means 'no caveats'.

allOf.description: A percent-only coverage record must be flagged, must name the measure it scraped, and must not smuggle in raw counts that would contradict it.

then.description: flags must be present and must carry 'percent_only'.
